title: Area and Perimeter: Polygons and Circles
seo_title: Grade 8 Area and Perimeter Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_code: Grade 8: 4.1 Area and perimeter of 2D shapes
standard_text: Use appropriate formulae to calculate perimeter and area of squares, rectangles, triangles and circles; calculate areas of polygons, to at least 2 decimal places, by decomposing into rectangles and/or triangles; use and convert between appropriate SI units.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 8 area and perimeter worksheets: triangles, trapeziums, kites, circumference and area of circles and composite shapes. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Triangle: A = ½ × b × h. Parallelogram: A = b × h. Trapezium: A = ½(a + b) × h.
  • Circumference: C = πd = 2πr. Area of a circle: A = πr².
  • Use π ≈ 3,14 or the π key.
  • Split composite shapes; subtract the area of a hole.

Examples

Example

A circle with diameter 10 cm

r = 5 cm

A = π × 5²

Answer: about 78,5 cm²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting ½Triangles and trapeziums need ½.
Diameter as radiusr = d ÷ 2.
C or A?Area uses r² and is in cm².
